test_title: PYST 35: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In lipid biochemistry, why do unsaturated fatty acids tend to be liquid at room temperature?

options.text: They form ionic bonds that prevent solidification.
The cis-double bonds introduce kinks, reducing van der Waals interactions.
Their double bonds increase molecular symmetry leading to less crystal packing.
They have lower molecular weights than saturated fatty acids.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The cis-double bonds introduce kinks, reducing van der Waals interactions.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Unsaturated fatty acids have **cis-double bonds** that introduce kinks in their hydrocarbon chains.
 
• These kinks prevent tight packing of the fatty acid molecules, thereby **reducing van der Waals interactions**.
 
• As a result, unsaturated fatty acids have **lower melting points** compared to saturated fatty acids, making them liquid at room temperature.
 
• The inability to tightly pack molecules leads to a more **fluid structure**, which is characteristic of oils derived from unsaturated fatty acids.
 
• The degree of unsaturation (number of double bonds) further influences the extent of fluidity in these molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Van der Waals interactions:**

 
 
• These are weak forces of attraction between molecules due to temporary dipoles.
 
• In saturated fatty acids, tight packing results in stronger van der Waals forces, contributing to solid state at room temperature.
 
 
 
• **Cis and trans configurations:**
 
 
• Cis-double bonds introduce bends or kinks in the fatty acid chains, while trans-double bonds allow linear structures.
 
• Trans fats behave more like saturated fats and are often solid at room temperature.
 
 
 
• **Saturated vs Unsaturated Fatty Acids:**
 
 
• Saturated fatty acids lack double bonds, allowing tighter molecular packing.
 
• Unsaturated fatty acids contain one or more double bonds, which disrupt packing and increase fluidity.
 
 
 
• **Role in cell membranes:**
 
 
• Unsaturated fatty acids contribute to membrane fluidity, essential for cellular functions.
 
• Phospholipids with unsaturated fatty acid tails are a key component of biological membranes.
 
 
 
• **Melting points of fatty acids:**
 
 
• Saturated fatty acids like stearic acid have higher melting points.
 
• Unsaturated fatty acids like oleic acid are liquid at room temperature due to disrupted packing.
